query: Consider the following context: High-entropy alloy (HEA) multilayers represent a promising class of advanced coating materials due to their superior mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and irradiation tolerance. However, the specific role of interface coherency on the creep behavior of HEA multilayers remains unclear. In that context, which material can be used for transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep mechanisms, and why?

generation.hypothesis: In HEA multilayers, inserting a thin, coherently bonded interfacial layer of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will mediate a smooth transition from diffusion‐mediated creep at high temperatures to dislocation‐mediated creep at lower temperatures by leveraging its intrinsic nanostructure and high dislocation density.
generation.material_initial_state: Standard HEA multilayers without a dedicated transitional interlayer.
generation.intervention: Introduce a thin interlayer (~nm-scale) of CoCrFeMnNi that forms coherent interfaces with adjacent HEA layers.
generation.conditions: Creep tests conducted over a broad temperature range spanning from ambient to high temperatures (e.g., 25°C to above 700°C) where diffusion and dislocation creep mechanisms become dominant.
generation.structural_mediator: The coherency of the CoCrFeMnNi interlayer with the surrounding HEA layers.
generation.mechanism: At lower temperatures, the coherent CoCrFeMnNi layer with its high dislocation density promotes dislocation-based creep (dislocation glide and pile-up), while at higher temperatures, its clean, coherent interfaces and stable nanostructure modulate grain-boundary diffusion, delaying the onset of diffusion-mediated creep. This dual capability provides a controlled transition between the two creep mechanisms.
generation.predicted_outcome: The multilayer system with the CoCrFeMnNi interlayer will exhibit improved creep resistance with a measurable shift in the dominant creep mechanism (from dislocation-mediated at lower temperatures to diffusion-mediated at higher temperatures) compared to a baseline multilayer without the interlayer.
generation.baseline: HEA multilayers without the CoCrFeMnNi transitional interlayer.
generation.boundary: The effect is expected to be significant only when the interlayer thickness and coherency are optimized; deviations lead either to premature transition or incoherent interfaces that do not mediate the desired creep mechanism change.
generation.uncertainty: The precise optimal thickness of the CoCrFeMnNi interlayer and the quantitative shift in creep mechanism activation are not fully known and require systematic experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of HEA multilayer coatings: one with a thin, intentionally coherent CoCrFeMnNi interlayer and a control set without the interlayer. Conduct creep experiments across a temperature series (e.g., 25°C to >700°C) while characterizing the microstructure and interface coherency with TEM and high-resolution microscopy, and measure creep strain rates and dislocation densities.
measurements: Creep strain rate as a function of temperature
Dislocation density via TEM or X-ray line profile analysis
Interface characterizations (coherency, lattice misfit) via HRTEM
Activation energy for creep mechanisms determined from strain rate changes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of the CoCrFeMnNi interlayer does not result in a statistically significant change in the temperature at which the transition from dislocation-mediated to diffusion-mediated creep is observed compared to the control, or if the interlayer does not maintain coherent interfaces under testing conditions, the hypothesis is invalidated.

Question: What are the temperature-dependent mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy additively manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM) compared to conventionally processed alloys?. System: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Selective laser melting (SLM) using pre-alloyed spherical powder (average diameter 27.2 µm); laser power 90 W, scan speed 600 mm/s, hatch space 80 µm, layer thickness 25 µm, volumetric energy density 75 J/mm³, 180° rotation scanning pattern, high-purity Ar atmosphere.. Test conditions: Compression tests at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C; initial strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; engineering strain limit 0.4; specimens preheated at 10 °C/min; MoS₂ lubricant used..
